take_homes: Interview the teammate about their job before I decide what to share, and pick the sharing route (context, skill, push, pull) by their outcome, not by what we have installed.
Most of my fourteen would be better served by push (a brief that lands where they look) than by getting a copy of my folder.
Writing the people plan next to the technical plan showed me how many roles are still unnamed. That gap, not the tooling, is what will stop the pilot.

monday.move: Message the pricing analyst who builds the usage-data spreadsheet and ask for 20 minutes on how she prepares the pilot-cohort numbers today. I show her nothing until she has answered. Then I test one assumption: that the brief lands in the channel she already reads.
monday.who: The analyst on the pricing working group who maintains the pilot-cohort spreadsheet. I also need to find out who owns the shared context folder.
monday.when: Message Monday morning; the 20 minutes before Wednesday.
monday.stop_condition: If she says she'd never open a brief and prefers to pull the numbers herself, I drop push for her and think about pull or a skill.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files; everyone keeps their own copy. The module names this kind of problem but doesn't solve it.

misconception.why: Prompts were hardly mentioned. What mattered was context, who owns the agent, and whether anyone picks it up. I still half think prompt skill helps, but it clearly isn't what stops fourteen people using this.

one_line: Useful if you have a team to bring along: you leave with one named person to talk to on Monday, but it says the same thing three times.
